passages.text: “At that time,” declares the LORD, “I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be My people.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
He makes a promise about the future.
He says, “At that time, I will be the God of all the families of Israel.
All the families of Israel will belong to Me.
They will be My people.”
passages.original: בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ־ לִ֥י לְעָֽם׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness when Israel went to find rest.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says these words.
Some people survived the sword.
These people are called the remnant.
These people traveled through the wilderness.
The LORD showed favor to these people in the wilderness.
Israel went to find rest.
The LORD gave rest to Israel.
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מָצָ֥א חֵן֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר עַ֖ם שְׂרִ֣ידֵי חָ֑רֶב הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: The LORD appeared to us in the past, saying: “I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
The LORD appeared to us long ago.
The LORD spoke to us.
The LORD said, “I have loved you with a love that never ends.
Because of this love, I have drawn you to Myself with kindness.
I have shown you faithful devotion.”
passages.original: מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י וְאַהֲבַ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ עַל־ כֵּ֖ן מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ חָֽסֶד׃

passages.text: Again I will build you, and you will be rebuilt, O Virgin Israel. Again you will take up your tambourines and go out in joyful dancing.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Israel.
Israel is called "Virgin Israel."
The LORD promises to build Israel again.
Israel will be rebuilt.
Israel will take up tambourines again.
Israel will go out in joyful dancing.
passages.original: ע֤וֹד אֶבְנֵךְ֙ וְֽנִבְנֵ֔ית בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֚וֹד תַּעְדִּ֣י תֻפַּ֔יִךְ וְיָצָ֖את בִּמְח֥וֹל מְשַׂחֲקִֽים׃

passages.text: Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; the farmers will plant and enjoy the fruit.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Israel.
God promised restoration.
You will plant vineyards again.
You will plant them on the hills of Samaria.
Farmers will plant these vineyards.
Farmers will enjoy the fruit.
passages.original: ע֚וֹד תִּטְּעִ֣י כְרָמִ֔ים בְּהָרֵ֖י שֹֽׁמְר֑וֹן נָטְע֥וּ נֹטְעִ֖ים וְחִלֵּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: For there will be a day when watchmen will call out on the hills of Ephraim, ‘Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!’ ”
passages.sermon:
Watchmen stand on the hills of Ephraim.
They look out and keep watch.
A day will come.
On that day, the watchmen will call out.
They will say, “Arise.
Let us go up to Zion.
Let us go to the LORD our God.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י יֶשׁ־ י֔וֹם קָרְא֥וּ נֹצְרִ֖ים בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃פ

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: “Sing with joy for Jacob; shout for the foremost of the nations! Make your praises heard, and say, ‘O LORD, save Your people, the remnant of Israel!’
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD gives a command.
Sing with joy for Jacob.
Jacob is the ancestor of Israel.
Shout for the foremost of the nations.
Israel is the foremost of the nations.
Make your praises heard.
Say these words:
O LORD, save Your people.
Save the remnant of Israel.
The remnant of Israel are those who remain.
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה רָנּ֤וּ לְיַֽעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְחָ֔ה וְצַהֲל֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם הַשְׁמִ֤יעוּ הַֽלְלוּ֙ וְאִמְר֔וּ הוֹשַׁ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶֽת־ עַמְּךָ֔ אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Behold, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the farthest parts of the earth, including the blind and the lame, expectant mothers and women in labor. They will return as a great assembly!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God promises to act.
God says, “I will bring them from the land of the north.
I will gather them from the farthest parts of the earth.
I will include the blind.
I will include the lame.
I will include expectant mothers.
I will include women in labor.
All of them will come together.
They will return as a great assembly.”
passages.original: הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אוֹתָ֜ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֗וֹן וְקִבַּצְתִּים֮ מִיַּרְכְּתֵי־ אָרֶץ֒ בָּ֚ם עִוֵּ֣ר וּפִסֵּ֔חַ הָרָ֥ה וְיֹלֶ֖דֶת יַחְדָּ֑ו קָהָ֥ל גָּד֖וֹל יָשׁ֥וּבוּ הֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: They will come with weeping, and by their supplication I will lead them; I will make them walk beside streams of waters, on a level path where they will not stumble. For I am Israel’s Father, and Ephraim is My firstborn.”
passages.sermon:
God is speaking to His people Israel.
God is their Father.
Ephraim is God's firstborn.
God says, "They will come with weeping."
They will pray and ask for help.
I will lead them because of their prayers.
I will guide them to streams of water.
I will make them walk on a straight path.
They will not stumble on this path.
passages.original: בִּבְכִ֣י יָבֹ֗אוּ וּֽבְתַחֲנוּנִים֮ אֽוֹבִילֵם֒ אֽוֹלִיכֵם֙ אֶל־ נַ֣חֲלֵי מַ֔יִם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָשָׁ֔ר לֹ֥א יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ בָּ֑הּ כִּֽי־ הָיִ֤יתִי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאָ֔ב וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא׃ס

passages.text: Hear, O nations, the word of the LORD, and proclaim it in distant coastlands: “The One who scattered Israel will gather them and keep them as a shepherd keeps his flock.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to all nations.
He commands everyone to listen to His word.
He tells people in distant lands to hear this message.
The LORD scattered Israel among the nations.
The LORD Himself will gather Israel again.
The LORD will protect Israel.
He will care for them as a shepherd cares for his flock.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֤וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְהַגִּ֥ידוּ בָאִיִּ֖ים מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק וְאִמְר֗וּ מְזָרֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְקַבְּצֶ֔נּוּ וּשְׁמָר֖וֹ כְּרֹעֶ֥ה עֶדְרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand that had overpowered him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD ransomed Jacob.
Jacob is the ancestor of Israel.
The LORD redeemed Jacob.
Jacob was in the hand of one stronger than him.
The LORD saved Jacob from that power.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ פָדָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹ֑ב וּגְאָל֕וֹ מִיַּ֖ד חָזָ֥ק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: They will come and shout for joy on the heights of Zion; they will be radiant over the bounty of the LORD— the grain, new wine, and oil, and the young of the flocks and herds. Their life will be like a well-watered garden, and never again will they languish.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel will come to Zion.
They will shout for joy on the high places of Zion.
They will rejoice because of the LORD’s goodness.
The LORD will give them grain.
The LORD will give them new wine.
The LORD will give them oil.
The LORD will give them young sheep and cattle.
Their lives will be like a garden that has plenty of water.
They will never be weak or sorrowful again.
passages.original: וּבָאוּ֮ וְרִנְּנ֣וּ בִמְרוֹם־ צִיּוֹן֒ וְנָהֲר֞וּ אֶל־ ט֣וּב יְהוָ֗ה עַל־ דָּגָן֙ וְעַל־ תִּירֹ֣שׁ וְעַל־ יִצְהָ֔ר וְעַל־ בְּנֵי־ צֹ֖אן וּבָקָ֑ר וְהָיְתָ֤ה נַפְשָׁם֙ כְּגַ֣ן רָוֶ֔ה וְלֹא־ יוֹסִ֥יפוּ לְדַאֲבָ֖ה עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Then the maidens will rejoice with dancing, young men and old as well. I will turn their mourning into joy, and give them comfort and joy for their sorrow.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God speaks to His people.
Young women will rejoice.
They will dance.
Young men will rejoice too.
Old men will rejoice with them.
God will change their mourning into joy.
God will comfort them.
God will give them joy instead of sorrow.
passages.original: אָ֣ז תִּשְׂמַ֤ח בְּתוּלָה֙ בְּמָח֔וֹל וּבַחֻרִ֥ים וּזְקֵנִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וְהָפַכְתִּ֨י אֶבְלָ֤ם לְשָׂשׂוֹן֙ וְנִ֣חַמְתִּ֔ים וְשִׂמַּחְתִּ֖ים מִיגוֹנָֽם׃

passages.text: I will fill the souls of the priests abundantly, and will fill My people with My goodness,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises to act.
The LORD will fill the priests.
The LORD will give the priests abundance.
The LORD will satisfy His people.
The LORD will give His people His goodness.
passages.original: וְרִוֵּיתִ֛י נֶ֥פֶשׁ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים דָּ֑שֶׁן וְעַמִּ֛י אֶת־ טוּבִ֥י יִשְׂבָּ֖עוּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and great weeping, Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
A voice comes from Ramah.
People hear mourning in Ramah.
There is great weeping in Ramah.
Rachel weeps for her children.
Rachel refuses to be comforted.
Her children are gone.
Her children are no more.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה ק֣וֹל בְּרָמָ֤ה נִשְׁמָע֙ נְהִי֙ בְּכִ֣י תַמְרוּרִ֔ים רָחֵ֖ל מְבַכָּ֣ה עַל־ בָּנֶ֑יהָ מֵאֲנָ֛ה לְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־ בָּנֶ֖יהָ כִּ֥י אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Keep your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for the reward for your work will come, declares the LORD. Then your children will return from the land of the enemy.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD commands.
Do not cry out in sorrow.
Do not let your eyes shed tears.
The LORD promises a reward for your work.
Your children will return from the land of the enemy.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה מִנְעִ֤י קוֹלֵךְ֙ מִבֶּ֔כִי וְעֵינַ֖יִךְ מִדִּמְעָ֑ה כִּי֩ יֵ֨שׁ שָׂכָ֤ר לִפְעֻלָּתֵךְ֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְשָׁ֖בוּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ אוֹיֵֽב׃

passages.text: So there is hope for your future, declares the LORD, and your children will return to their own land.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD gives hope.
You have hope for your future.
The LORD promises this.
Your children will return.
They will come back to their own land.
passages.original: וְיֵשׁ־ תִּקְוָ֥ה לְאַחֲרִיתֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁ֥בוּ בָנִ֖ים לִגְבוּלָֽם׃ס

passages.text: I have surely heard Ephraim’s moaning: ‘You disciplined me severely, like an untrained calf. Restore me, that I may return, for You are the LORD my God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD hears Ephraim.
Ephraim is moaning.
Ephraim says, “You disciplined me.”
The discipline was severe.
Ephraim was like an untrained calf.
Ephraim asks, “Restore me.”
Ephraim wants to return.
Ephraim says, “You are the LORD my God.”
passages.original: שָׁמ֣וֹעַ שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ מִתְנוֹדֵ֔ד יִסַּרְתַּ֙נִי֙ וָֽאִוָּסֵ֔ר כְּעֵ֖גֶל לֹ֣א לֻמָּ֑ד הֲשִׁיבֵ֣נִי וְאָשׁ֔וּבָה כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: After I returned, I repented; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh in grief. I was ashamed and humiliated because I bore the disgrace of my youth.’
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is speaking.
Ephraim is a tribe of Israel.
Ephraim says, “After I returned, I repented.
After I learned, I struck my thigh in grief.
I was ashamed.
I was also humiliated.
I carried the disgrace of my youth.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אַחֲרֵ֤י שׁוּבִי֙ נִחַ֔מְתִּי וְאַֽחֲרֵי֙ הִוָּ֣דְעִ֔י סָפַ֖קְתִּי עַל־ יָרֵ֑ךְ בֹּ֚שְׁתִּי וְגַם־ נִכְלַ֔מְתִּי כִּ֥י נָשָׂ֖אתִי חֶרְפַּ֥ת נְעוּרָֽי׃

passages.text: Is not Ephraim a precious son to Me, a delightful child? Though I often speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore My heart yearns for him; I have great compassion for him,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about Ephraim.
Ephraim is a tribe of Israel.
The LORD says, “Ephraim is My precious son.
Ephraim is a delightful child to Me.
I often speak against Ephraim.
But I still remember Ephraim.
My heart longs deeply for Ephraim.
I have great compassion for Ephraim.
I, the LORD, declare this.”
passages.original: הֲבֵן֩ יַקִּ֨יר לִ֜י אֶפְרַ֗יִם אִ֚ם יֶ֣לֶד שַׁעֲשֻׁעִ֔ים כִּֽי־ מִדֵּ֤י דַבְּרִי֙ בּ֔וֹ זָכֹ֥ר אֶזְכְּרֶ֖נּוּ ע֑וֹד עַל־ כֵּ֗ן הָמ֤וּ מֵעַי֙ ל֔וֹ רַחֵ֥ם אֲ‍ֽרַחֲמֶ֖נּוּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “Set up the roadmarks, establish the signposts. Keep the highway in mind, the road you have traveled. Return, O Virgin Israel, return to these cities of yours.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God calls Israel "Virgin Israel."
God tells Israel to return home.
God says, "Set up roadmarks for yourself."
God says, "Establish signposts for yourself."
God says, "Pay attention to the highway."
God says, "Remember the road you traveled."
God says, "Return, Virgin Israel."
God says, "Return to your cities."
God wants Israel to come back to her own land.
passages.original: הַצִּ֧יבִי לָ֣ךְ צִיֻּנִ֗ים שִׂ֤מִי לָךְ֙ תַּמְרוּרִ֔ים שִׁ֣תִי לִבֵּ֔ךְ לַֽמְסִלָּ֖ה דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָלָכְתִּי שׁ֚וּבִי בְּתוּלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֻׁ֖בִי אֶל־ עָרַ֥יִךְ אֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: How long will you wander, O faithless daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing in the land— a woman will shelter a man.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Israel.
Israel is like a faithless daughter.
The LORD asks, “How long will you wander?”
The LORD has created something new in the land.
A woman will shelter a man.
passages.original: עַד־ מָתַי֙ תִּתְחַמָּקִ֔ין הַבַּ֖ת הַשּֽׁוֹבֵבָ֑ה כִּֽי־ בָרָ֨א יְהוָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ נְקֵבָ֖ה תְּס֥וֹבֵֽב גָּֽבֶר׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “When I restore them from captivity, they will once again speak this word in the land of Judah and in its cities: ‘May the LORD bless you, O righteous dwelling place, O holy mountain.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
He speaks these words.
He says, “I will restore my people from captivity.
They will return to the land of Judah.
They will live in its cities again.
They will say this word once more.
‘May the LORD bless you.
You are a righteous dwelling place.
You are a holy mountain.’”
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ע֣וֹד יֹאמְר֞וּ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבְעָרָ֔יו בְּשׁוּבִ֖י אֶת־ שְׁבוּתָ֑ם יְבָרֶכְךָ֧ יְהוָ֛ה נְוֵה־ צֶ֖דֶק הַ֥ר הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: And Judah and all its cities will dwell together in the land, the farmers and those who move with the flocks, for I will refresh the weary soul and replenish all who are weak.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God promises restoration.
Judah will live in the land.
All the cities of Judah will live together.
Farmers will live there.
People who move with their flocks will live there.
God will refresh every weary soul.
God will fill every weak soul with strength.
passages.original: וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ בָ֛הּ יְהוּדָ֥ה וְכָל־ עָרָ֖יו יַחְדָּ֑ו אִכָּרִ֕ים וְנָסְע֖וּ בַּעֵֽדֶר׃ כִּ֥י הִרְוֵ֖יתִי נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וְכָל־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ דָּאֲבָ֖ה מִלֵּֽאתִי׃

passages.text: At this I awoke and looked around. My sleep had been most pleasant to me.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is the speaker.
Jeremiah had a vision from God.
Jeremiah woke up.
Jeremiah looked around.
Jeremiah felt that his sleep was very pleasant.
passages.original: עַל־ זֹ֖את הֱקִיצֹ֣תִי וָאֶרְאֶ֑ה וּשְׁנָתִ֖י עָ֥רְבָה לִּֽי׃ס

passages.text: “The days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and of beast.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says, “The days are coming.”
I will act in those days.
I will sow the house of Israel.
I will sow the house of Judah.
I will use the seed of man.
I will use the seed of beast.
I will plant people and animals among them.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְזָרַעְתִּ֗י אֶת־ בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה זֶ֥רַע אָדָ֖ם וְזֶ֥רַע בְּהֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: Just as I watched over them to uproot and tear down, to demolish, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks these words.
The LORD watched over Israel and Judah.
The LORD acted to uproot them.
The LORD acted to tear them down.
The LORD acted to demolish them.
The LORD acted to destroy them.
The LORD brought disaster upon them.
The LORD did all these things with care and attention.
Now the LORD will watch over Israel and Judah again.
The LORD will build them up.
The LORD will plant them.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֞ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר שָׁקַ֣דְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לִנְת֧וֹשׁ וְלִנְת֛וֹץ וְלַהֲרֹ֖ס וּלְהַאֲבִ֣יד וּלְהָרֵ֑עַ כֵּ֣ן אֶשְׁקֹ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם לִבְנ֥וֹת וְלִנְט֖וֹעַ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “In those days, it will no longer be said: ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke about a future time.
He said, “In those days, people will not say this saying anymore.
They will not say, ‘The fathers ate sour grapes.
The children’s teeth became set on edge.’”
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם לֹא־ יֹאמְר֣וּ ע֔וֹד אָב֖וֹת אָ֣כְלוּ בֹ֑סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י בָנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה׃

passages.text: Instead, each will die for his own iniquity. If anyone eats the sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel and Judah.
God says each person is responsible for his own sin.
Each person will die for his own iniquity.
If a person eats sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.
passages.original: כִּ֛י אִם־ אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנ֖וֹ יָמ֑וּת כָּל־ הָֽאָדָ֛ם הָאֹכֵ֥ל הַבֹּ֖סֶר תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו׃ס

passages.text: Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises a new covenant.
The LORD will make this covenant with Israel.
The LORD will make this covenant with Judah.
The LORD says these days are coming.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְכָרַתִּ֗י אֶת־ בֵּ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְאֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּרִ֥ית חֲדָשָֽׁה׃

passages.text: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt— a covenant they broke, though I was a husband to them,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD made a covenant with the ancestors of Israel and Judah.
The LORD took their ancestors by the hand.
The LORD led them out of the land of Egypt.
Their ancestors broke the LORD’s covenant.
The LORD was like a husband to them.
The new covenant will not be like that old covenant.
passages.original: לֹ֣א כַבְּרִ֗ית אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּרַ֙תִּי֙ אֶת־ אֲבוֹתָ֔ם בְּיוֹם֙ הֶחֱזִיקִ֣י בְיָדָ֔ם לְהוֹצִיאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֖רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר־ הֵ֜מָּה הֵפֵ֣רוּ אֶת־ בְּרִיתִ֗י וְאָנֹכִ֛י בָּעַ֥לְתִּי בָ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “But this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD. I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD will make a new covenant.
The LORD will make this covenant with the house of Israel.
The LORD will do this after those days.
The LORD will put His law inside them.
The LORD will write His law on their hearts.
The LORD will be their God.
They will be His people.
passages.original: כִּ֣י זֹ֣את הַבְּרִ֡ית אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶכְרֹת֩ אֶת־ בֵּ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אַחֲרֵ֨י הַיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵם֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה נָתַ֤תִּי אֶת־ תּֽוֹרָתִי֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔ם וְעַל־ לִבָּ֖ם אֶכְתֲּבֶ֑נָּה וְהָיִ֤יתִי לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ־ לִ֥י לְעָֽם׃

passages.text: No longer will each man teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks these words.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD says a time will come.
People will not teach their neighbors about God.
People will not tell their brothers, “Know the LORD.”
Everyone will know the LORD.
The least person will know the LORD.
The greatest person will know the LORD.
The LORD promises this.
The LORD will forgive their sins.
The LORD will not remember their wrongdoings anymore.
passages.original: וְלֹ֧א יְלַמְּד֣וּ ע֗וֹד אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֜הוּ וְאִ֤ישׁ אֶת־ אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר דְּע֖וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־ כוּלָּם֩ יֵדְע֨וּ אוֹתִ֜י לְמִקְטַנָּ֤ם וְעַד־ גְּדוֹלָם֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֤י אֶסְלַח֙ לַֽעֲוֺנָ֔ם וּלְחַטָּאתָ֖ם לֹ֥א אֶזְכָּר־ עֽוֹד׃ס

passages.text: Thus says the LORD, who gives the sun for light by day, who sets in order the moon and stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar—the LORD of Hosts is His name: “Only if this fixed order departed from My presence, declares the LORD, would Israel’s descendants ever cease to be a nation before Me.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD gives the sun to shine by day.
The LORD sets the moon and stars to shine by night.
The LORD stirs up the sea.
The waves of the sea roar because of Him.
His name is the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD says this:
If this fixed order ever leaves My presence,
then Israel’s descendants would stop being a nation before Me.
This will never happen.
Israel will always remain a nation before the LORD.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה נֹתֵ֥ן שֶׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ לְא֣וֹר יוֹמָ֔ם חֻקֹּ֛ת יָרֵ֥חַ וְכוֹכָבִ֖ים לְא֣וֹר לָ֑יְלָה רֹגַ֤ע הַיָּם֙ וַיֶּהֱמ֣וּ גַלָּ֔יו יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ אִם־ יָמֻ֜שׁוּ הַחֻקִּ֥ים הָאֵ֛לֶּה מִלְּפָנַ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה גַּם֩ זֶ֨רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל יִשְׁבְּת֗וּ מִֽהְי֥וֹת גּ֛וֹי לְפָנַ֖י כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Only if the heavens above could be measured and the foundations of the earth below searched out would I reject all of Israel’s descendants because of all they have done,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD says this.
People cannot measure the heavens above.
People cannot search out the foundations of the earth below.
Only if people could do these things, says the LORD,
then I would reject all the descendants of Israel because of all they have done.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִם־ יִמַּ֤דּוּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה וְיֵחָקְר֥וּ מֽוֹסְדֵי־ אֶ֖רֶץ לְמָ֑טָּה גַּם־ אֲנִ֞י אֶמְאַ֨ס בְּכָל־ זֶ֧רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַֽל־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “The days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when this city will be rebuilt for Me, from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises a future event.
The LORD says, “The days are coming.”
The LORD will cause the city to be rebuilt.
People will rebuild the city for the LORD.
The rebuilding will start at the tower of Hananel.
The rebuilding will continue to the Corner Gate.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥יםִָּ֖ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְנִבְנְתָ֤ה הָעִיר֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה מִמִּגְדַּ֥ל חֲנַנְאֵ֖ל שַׁ֥עַר הַפִּנָּֽה׃

passages.text: The measuring line will once again stretch out straight to the hill of Gareb and then turn toward Goah.
passages.sermon: The measuring line will stretch out again.\r\nIt will go straight to the hill of Gareb.\r\nThen it will turn toward Goah.
passages.original: וְיָצָ֨א ע֜וֹד קְוֵה הַמִּדָּה֙ נֶגְדּ֔וֹ עַ֖ל גִּבְעַ֣ת גָּרֵ֑ב וְנָסַ֖ב גֹּעָֽתָה׃

passages.text: The whole valley of the dead bodies and ashes, and all the fields as far as the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate to the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will never again be uprooted or demolished.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeremiah the prophet.
God promised to restore Jerusalem.
The valley contains dead bodies and ashes.
All the fields reach as far as the Kidron Valley.
The land stretches to the corner of the Horse Gate on the east.
God will make all this land holy to Him.
No one will ever uproot this land again.
No one will ever destroy it again.
This promise will last forever.
passages.original: וְכָל־ הָעֵ֣מֶק הַפְּגָרִ֣ים׀ וְהַדֶּ֡שֶׁן וְכָֽל־ הַשְּׁרֵמוֹת עַד־ נַ֨חַל קִדְר֜וֹן עַד־ פִּנַּ֨ת שַׁ֤עַר הַסּוּסִים֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־ יִנָּתֵ֧שׁ וְֽלֹא־ יֵהָרֵ֛ס ע֖וֹד לְעוֹלָֽם׃ס
